name: Celery juice diet

card.summary: Drinking fresh celery juice daily, promoted for clearer, calmer skin and general health.
card.note: Juicing removes fibre; celery contains vitamin K, relevant to some blood thinners.

quick.overview:
The celery juice routine involves drinking juiced celery, typically on an empty stomach each morning. Followers say it clears skin, reduces bloating and boosts energy, which they connect to looking healthier.

The practice was popularised by Anthony William, the "Medical Medium". Dietitians quoted in coverage note that studies of celery benefits involve whole stalks, and no clinical trial has tested the juice routine itself.
quick.how: People blend or juice celery stalks and drink the result, often first thing in the morning, sometimes alongside other produce. Reported timelines for skin changes in community posts vary.
quick.risks: Celery is a low-risk food for most people, but its vitamin K can interfere with warfarin-type medicines, and juicing strips fibre. Reliance on the routine in place of medical care for skin or other conditions is a concern raised by physicians.

lead: The celery juice diet is a wellness trend in which people drink fresh celery juice daily, with followers describing clearer skin, less inflammation and better digestion as the appeal [1].

Anthony William, who writes as the "Medical Medium", says he originated the trend and calls the juice a miracle drink; his first book appeared in 2015 [1]. He describes his advice as coming from a spirit connection and states he holds no medical certifications [1].

Dietitians note that celery's fibre is lost in juicing, that benefits seen in studies came from whole stalks, and that celery's vitamin K can interfere with medications such as warfarin [1]. No clinical trial of the celery juice routine for skin has been identified.

chain: Daily celery juice replaces other drinks
Followers report calmer, clearer skin and less bloating
angle.text: Followers drink celery juice daily and report clearer skin and a fresher look. These outcomes are reported by practitioners rather than measured in trials.

paras: The routine centres on juiced celery, usually consumed alone. Proponents present it as a daily cleanse-style habit [1].

William began promoting supplements and herbs in 1985 and published eight books, several of them bestsellers, with roughly 3 million Instagram followers as of 2021 [1]. He wrote for Goop, which drew criticism in 2018 [1].
William attributes chronic illness to the Epstein-Barr virus and recommends celery juice and vitamin B12 [1]. Followers extend this to skin and appearance benefits.

Reviewers quoted on the page say no scientific evidence supports the health claims made for the juice [1]. Physicians including OB/GYN Jennifer Gunter have warned that following such advice can delay diagnoses [1].

timeline.event: William begins promoting supplements and herbs [1].
Goop's promotion of William draws criticism [1].

lore.intro: Celery juice is discussed in wellness communities as a morning ritual for skin and digestion [1].

claims.claim: Celery juice clears skin and reduces inflammation
claims.believers: Followers of the Medical Medium report calmer skin and less bloating after daily use [1].
claims.experts: Dietitians say benefits seen in studies came from whole celery and no clinical evidence supports the health claims for the juice [1].
